correctness.rationale: All three positive part sizes, synchronous open-neighborhood majority and tie retention are explicit. A changing part necessarily toggles uniformly, a sole toggler is impossible, two togglers must be opposite and equal-sized with exact strict central-binomial weight window, and three togglers exist exactly with a unique largest part. All cases are disjoint and exhaustive. Independent direct-state and weighted aggregate checks agree on 89 and 1,137 triples, respectively; only the analytic proof establishes the infinite claim.

value.rationale: A complete natural three-parameter primitive-orbit invariant exhibits a sharp symmetry-breaking contrast: exactly one temporal oscillation for every pairwise-distinct size triple, but potentially exponential multiplicities when two part sizes coincide. The explicit central binomial interval and odd/even boundary quantify this structural transition; this is not a mere fixed-point recount or a routine table recomputation.
